comments.text:
Born and raised a rock's throw from Canada along the St. John's River. In the heart of potato country. I remember watching my Red Sox's opening day in Fenway in the living room. And at the same time looking outside into the yard, seeing 8' snowbanks at the edge of US1-A. Right then and there this wasn't the place for me. At 18, I hit the road. Tried of having anything to do with potatoes. 
Ended up in central Maine (Lewiston) and started my life time working years as a proud ship builder at Bath Iron Works. Did 30 years freezing on cold steel plate. Retired at an age of 54, and now happily living out my life in sunny Florida. Thank you for the video of my home State. Brings back memories, especially when you spoke of cords of firewood. That I do not miss.

replies.author: @HappyTravel99
replies.text: What an incredible life journey! ❤️ From the snowy potato fields of northern Maine to 30 years of hard work at Bath Iron Works, and now enjoying the sunshine in Florida! We can certainly understand why you don't miss those freezing winters or the endless firewood! 😊 It's wonderful that our video brought back so many memories of your home state. Thank you so much for sharing your story with us. Wishing you a long, healthy, and happy retirement filled with sunshine and beautiful days! ❤️🙏

comments.author: @ZivErisaar
comments.text: (1)  I really enjoyed the history, the ruggedness of the land which of course makes the people stronger or they leave, I adore mountains, lakes, and coasts & wish I could live even more rural and come from a family of fishermen - so I am in awe.  I'm the romantic who loves the outdoors but enjoys it from a comfy, fire warmed room with a wall of glass to look out.  Once you live rural, can stock a pantry so you only shop once a month...& love nature instead of fighting it... you won't go back to big city life.  I worked hard to find a rural farm & still dream of a "perfect place" (more affordable I left Seattle & Chesapeake, VA for a cheaper way of living despite missing the land & sea.) with a beautiful countryside, sea sides to visit, good neighbors who you can trust....yes I know how possessive fishermen are! lol  it's their livelihood.  Leaving cars, machines, and homes unlocked...is a treasure.  I loved the laws that changed because the people complained...this is how you do it instead of allowing minority vote corruption in.  The majority voice of the people must always win. This video gave me a lot of teary eyes & smiles and I hope the new influx of young folks bring the economy alive with possibilities without destroying the romance and the beauty of those who lived there before them and who are enjoying retired life now.

comments.author: @ValerieFeagin
comments.text: I first arrived here with my family in the late summer of 1969, shortly before my first birthday, from Tennessee.  We left for Louisiana in 1981, but visited in the summers for years afterward.  When my father retired in 2004, my parents returned and lived the rest of their lives here - my mother died in 2022 and my father in 2025, and they are buried together in Kent's Hill Cemetery.  I returned fir good in 2014 when my ex-wife and I separated, and I plan to die here as well.  I live in Hancock County, the Down East region and the country of my heart.  All the years I was gone I missed Maine as one misses an old love, a first love, and without condition despite its flaws.  I am from away, but this is my true home. ❤❤❤❤❤
